judged_text: The saveChanges action is unreachable — no template in the diff wires it — and its body sends an empty payload (update({})) to the no-op update endpoint. A future maintainer wiring a save button inherits a stub that submits no data to a controller that ignores it anyway, and reviewers reading the controller are misled into believing an embedding-settings save flow exists.

adjudication.rationale: In the new Ember controller `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`, `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` with an empty payload. In the new template `app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/embedding.hbs`, there is no button or UI element invoking `saveChanges` (only `addHost` is wired via `{{d-button ... action="addHost"}}`, and per-host actions are in the `embeddable-host` component). On the server, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is a no-op that just re-renders the serializer without persisting anything. This is not a current functional defect (since nothing calls it), but it is dead/stubbed flow that can mislead maintainers/reviewers into thinking a settings save path exists.
